_about: Needles: one short, distinctive literal string per hard-won fact absorbed into the
plugin artifacts. `scripts/check-needles.py` asserts each one is present SOMEWHERE in
the corpus (plugins/**/*.md). Presence is asserted corpus-wide, never per file, so
content is free to move between artifacts — that is the point: the gate proves a fact
survived a restructure, it does not freeze the layout.
Adding a needle: pick a phrase that could only survive if the FACT survives — a coined
term, a literal command, a measured number, a distinctive noun phrase. Not a full
sentence (legitimate rewording breaks it) and not a common word (it passes by accident).
Verify it is present before committing; the gate refuses an absent needle.
Removing a needle: only with the deliberate decision that the fact no longer applies,
recorded in the commit message. A red gate is not a reason to delete the entry.

_fields.needle: Required. The literal substring asserted present in at least one corpus file.
_fields.issue: Originating ai-learning issue number, or null where the absorbing commit closed a batch and the individual attribution is not recoverable.
_fields.commit: The branch commit that absorbed the fact. `git show <sha>` carries the full rationale and the `Closes #…` set — see `_sources`.
_fields.was_in: DOCUMENTATION ONLY — the artifact this needle lived in when it was pinned. Never asserted. A starting point for a search, and expected to go stale as content moves.
_fields.note: Required. One line naming the fact the needle guards, so a red gate teaches instead of just failing.
_fields.file: OPTIONAL and rare. Repo-relative path. Present only where the LOCATION is itself the fact — then the needle must appear in that exact file. Do not add it to make a needle 'more precise'; it defeats the corpus-wide design.

needles.needle: ## 1 — A verdict is evidence only about what it actually executed
needles.note: Fact 1's heading. File-pinned deliberately: six artifacts cite it as '§1', so the numbered section is an addressable anchor and may not migrate.

needles.needle: ## 3 — An inherited statement is a claim with a provenance and an expiry
needles.note: Fact 3's heading. File-pinned for the same reason as fact 1 — verify-build and design-multi cite '§3' by number.

needles.needle: a gate states its blind spot in the same breath as its verdict
needles.note: The rule fact 1 exists to state: 'green' with no named blind spot is a claim, not a result.

needles.needle: a negative result is evidence only if the probe could have produced a positive
needles.note: The positive-control corollary — every absence claim (zero callers, nothing drifted) ships with something the probe must flag.
Why reassuring-failing checks ('no errors in ten minutes, therefore green') are the ones that need a positive control.

needles.needle: An unspecified seam adjacent to a specified one
needles.note: Fact 4 — the highest-risk place in a design, because the specified rule is exactly what gets reused in the gap.
A run that executed nothing exits 0. Inconclusive, never green, never a baseline. Restated by test-runner and verify-build.

needles.needle: stops parsing options at the first operand
needles.note: Probe hygiene: BSD getopt turns a trailing `--include` into a filename — prints nothing, exits 0, no stderr.
/start emits the baseline itself; without it every later step re-derives the base's pre-existing failures (fleet lanes, in parallel).
The measurement behind 'capture the baseline on a freshly built tree' — unresolved .d.ts cascades into ordinary-looking type errors.
A predicate claimed single-source-of-truth must fail one test per declared consumer; a shortfall means a second inline copy exists.
Set `passes: true` in the same turn as the commit — one lane sat on six committed slices with a state file reading slicesDone: 1.
Bash backgrounds a gate at the 600 s ceiling against your instruction; a subagent awaiting a backgrounded job deadlocks permanently.
An assertion reading PATH/HOME/TZ/locale/git-config has a verdict that is a property of who ran it.

needles.needle: Never negative-test a guard by mutating tracked files
needles.note: Prove a guard fails on bad input in a throwaway scratch dir — never end a turn with a deliberate mutation in the tree.

needles.needle: "none" is a valid answer, the field is not
needles.note: The executor's issues/deviations field is required output — it is routed verbatim into the verifier and is the cheapest defect-catch in the flow.
A load-flaky failure untouched by the slice's diff is an environment artifact, named as such — not a slice RED that triggers executor churn.
All three agents stop asking for a relay: the dispatching agent reads their return value directly. Present in executor, verifier and test-runner.

needles.needle: PASS-with-follow-ups is not available for a named mitigation
needles.note: A finding leaving a design-named mitigation unverified is RETRY, not a follow-up — parking it silently un-mitigates a consciously accepted risk.
A background wake arrives wrapped in an unsuppressable platform refusal; a text-review pass passes the design and the mechanism deadlocks.
The falsification table — the verifier's required output shape, covering the design docs' claims and not only the diff's.

needles.needle: paraphrased identifier is indistinguishable from a real one
needles.note: Quote symbols as the source spells them — a paraphrased identifier is indistinguishable from a real one until you grep. (Re-pinned 2026-09-05: the constraint-shaped rewrite in 1aa0c3c kept the fact and dropped the literal — the earlier needle was `parseAmountToMinorUnits`.)
State what a count counts, never 'five call sites'. Restated in design-multi and EVIDENCE §3.

Check the mechanism behind a ticket's rationale: a package 'blocked on publishing 1.4.0' had never been published at any version. (Re-pinned 2026-09-05: the constraint-shaped rewrite in 1aa0c3c kept the fact and dropped the literal — the earlier needle was `gh api /orgs/<org>/packages`.)

The second pass verifies a resolved block's reasoning, not that its cited sites still read as quoted — zero drift reads as nothing to check. (Re-pinned 2026-09-05: the constraint-shaped rewrite in 1aa0c3c kept the fact and dropped the literal — the earlier needle was `prose fitting is not the claim being true`.)
The design-doc section name that /plan and /build consume as explicit non-guidance. A section nobody emits is a silence that gets generalized.

needles.needle: could a fresh session holding only this repo
needles.note: Step 4's self-containment gate — a step may not hand off state living only in its own context, and this fails worse the better the session was.

needles.needle: no user to approve, by construction
needles.note: /plan's unattended branch — a literal reading of the human-review gate stalls every fleet lane at this step.
/design-multi greps for its own past output before dispatching — the one command guaranteed to meet its own work, and otherwise blind to it.

needles.needle: The emit precedes the critique deliberately
needles.note: critique's terminal-looking verdict outcompetes a trailing 'then emit'; two of three agents once ended their turn with no files written.
A task-completion notification is never evidence the agent produced anything — stat the files from disk before collecting a unit.
The third state beyond apply-or-skip for a glossary/ADR delta describing code that has not landed yet.
Three lanes once picked the same ADR number: different filenames, no conflict, clean merge. The orchestrator allocates, lanes never self-number.
The :v2 resolved-block readiness field. Without it an unattended lane picks up a deferred/blocked/umbrella unit and may open a bad PR.
A two-parent merge is the orchestrator's, not the child's — a base that does not compile surfaces its failures deep inside the child.
A reused worktree's .work/ is archived, not deleted: those buffers hold the learnings.md that step 6 exists to rescue.
Compute base-sensitive recon against the pinned BASE, never a working-dir grep whose HEAD has drifted from it.
Size --max-parallel by memory, not cores: past some N the fleet falls off a cliff, not a slope (95 s alone vs >38 min under load).
Address every message from agents.yaml, never from recall — reconstructing the map from dispatch order misrouted two corrections in one run.

needles.needle: terminal state and a positive control
needles.note: A stall detector without a terminal state cries wolf exactly when the run is going well, and gets muted right before it would have been useful.

needles.needle: Failed to resolve entry for package
needles.note: 'install' is not 'ready' — workspace deps resolve through a gitignored build/, so a fresh worktree needs a build before any agent is dispatched.
A child cut at build-complete is stranded on a base its parent then fixes; record the tip and forward-merge after the parent's verify-build.
A directive carries the constraint, never the expression — this one was implemented faithfully and double-billed a metering period.
Mechanical-guard sweep: enumerate every surface that can set the dispatch field. A sibling MCP surface forwarded it and disarmed the guard.

needles.needle: 72 lines below a line the PR had just fixed
needles.note: Claim-correction sweep: sweep the belief in synonyms, and re-sweep every file the PR itself edited — a self-contradicting file is worse than neither fix.
Merge-ripple sweep: new files conflict with nothing, so they appear in no conflict list — an added oracle merged green and tested nothing.
A green *partial* inventory reads as full coverage — compare the runner's reported file count against the repo's test files on disk.
A stacked child keeps pointing at a merged branch; merging it there returns exit 0, shows MERGED, and delivers nothing to the default branch.
A control byte in a source literal makes git call the file binary — grep returning nothing on a file you just edited is the earlier tell.
critique's input contract: hand the lenses verified facts, not a summary. Restatement means the input was too abstract, not that the design was sound.
The no-ADRs-yet default must match what vertical-slicing and verify-build render; it fires once per repo and sets a convention forever.
Proposed node ids do not derive the way extracted ones do — read the returned nodeIds instead of guessing a whole batch correctly.
The grill probe for any design leaning on a background task's exit re-invoking a session — it must explicitly disarm the platform refusal.
A recorded agentId dies with its session — which is precisely the situation a handoff exists to serve. Carry what a fresh dispatch needs.

needles.needle: gate that never fired is indistinguishable from a gate that cannot fire
needles.note: Order a self-enforcing slice so a later slice in the same PR is its first live subject. Also stated in verify-build step 4.
`onStarted` is not a queue: under the start-first boot order a bare `if (draining) return` silently drops every declaration after the first.
A complete-state projector write needs replace; the default merge can add and overwrite but never delete a key.
MemoryDb's upsert takes no options argument at all, so it silently ignores replace — the harness cannot even express the bug.
A new PolicyBuilder policy emits an internal operation route with no HTTP surface, and generate-all fails hard until it has a capability entry.
Drive a standalone cron poll policy through a real cron tick; a bare pollFn(ports) call dispatches a command that never reaches the pipeline.

needles.needle: dedup per-stream on version, NEVER on global position
needles.note: The one dedup rule: a global position high-water mark drops exactly the gap-recovered events, silently re-creating a dropped-event bug.
The dedup key is a per-stream last-applied version watermark; per-stream order makes it sufficient, so no consumer needs to remember every event id.
A skipped duplicate must still answer 2xx — an error makes the outbox retry it forever (retry storm) instead of setting the dispatched bit.
The four duplicate causes (a)-(d): crash-before-SETBIT, lost HTTP response, operator replay, and the unfenced cross-process owner that only appears after scale-out.

needles.needle: iff the dispatched bit was already set
needles.note: The exact definition of event.metadata.isRedelivery — true only where the outbox is re-sending an already-committed position, i.e. only operator replay.
isRedelivery is never set on a genuine first delivery, which is what makes suppressing an effect on it safe — and it is silent on the crash/retry paths.
A non-idempotent external effect needs the watermark committed atomically with it, or its own idempotency key; isRedelivery does not replace that work.
Guard order at the boundary: isRedelivery-skip first, then B/C dedup — isRedelivery is a no-op precisely on the crash-window duplicate, which is version > watermark.
The A/B/C layer model's B layer: a durable event.id-keyed checkpoint, distinct from the aggregate invariant (A) and the reconcile-by-natural-key (C).
Partial-progress redelivery: seed `remaining` from the source aggregate's recorded progress, never by re-walking live downstream balances.
The soft-delete trap: stateExists() does not protect a soft-deleted aggregate, so a terminal command re-emits its event on redelivery.
A blind processed-events ledger is justified only when the external effect is both non-idempotent AND non-reconcilable; otherwise reconcile by natural key.
Plain atomicIncrement is not redelivery-idempotent; an accumulating cross-stream counter needs a deterministic-id contribution ledger and delta-only increments.
Brand-new-row bootstrap: identity-only upsert plus per-field CAS init with op:'notExists' — a skeleton-of-zeros upsert loses a racing increment.

needles.needle: operator does not exist: text @> jsonb
needles.note: An array-of-string field queried with op:'contains' needs { strategy: 'gin' }; the default strategy materializes a text column and fails at runtime.
`.produces([])` crashes endpoint registration; a side-effect-only command declares one possible event and returns [] from the handler.
At-most-one-in-flight is a UNIQUE-constraint side-write acquired in the command transaction and released by every terminal handler — a missed one is the stuck-lock bug.
The safe contrast to persisted-field renames: PV3 derives stream/route/subscription identity from the filename, so renaming code symbols is safe. Do not over-apply the rule.
ddd-patterns is a hub plus six references; the trigger table is what gets the pointer followed. Lose it and six files are orphaned with nothing erroring.

needles.needle: A closing keyword binds to exactly one
needles.note: GitHub closes only the first issue after each Closes keyword. `Closes #56 #62 #63` closed #56 and left the rest open — 80 referenced issues became 7 closures and 73 stragglers, with the PR MERGED and CI green. Fails in the reassuring direction; the only tell is a backlog count.

needles.needle: writes the eval scenario in the same pass
needles.note: A split ships with its behavioral scenario, because every presence gate is corpus-wide by design and therefore green whether the pointer is ever opened or not. The pass that makes the split is the last moment anyone knows what the pointer was for. (Re-pinned 2026-09-05: the constraint-shaped rewrite in 1aa0c3c kept the fact and dropped the literal — the earlier needle was `the same pass writes the eval scenario`.)

needles.needle: A split you can delete beats a split you have to verify forever
needles.note: The split floor: below it a split spends loading probability and buys no attention relief. A 468-word skill with 668+351-word references — both passing their scenarios — was inlined and the splits deleted.

needles.needle: Split by trigger, never by topic
needles.note: Content may leave an artifact only when its loading is gated on a condition something already evaluates and acts on. 'Fleet mechanics' is a topic and splits unsafely; 'this unit checks out 2+ repos' is a trigger and splits safely.

needles.needle: Explanation may be referenced. Behavior may not
needles.note: The test for whether a reference file is the right instrument: ask what happens when the pointer is NOT followed. Losing only the why is safe (EVIDENCE.md); silently doing the wrong thing is not.
Behavior that must leave a parent goes to a subagent, not a reference file — fresh context, dispatched at the moment it applies. Worktree provisioning left /start-multi this way.
CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset in a command's bash block; it expands to empty and the failure reads as a missing file. Plugin executables go in bin/, which IS on PATH keyed by version.

needles.needle: Every millisecond is classified, never subtracted
needles.note: Run timing cannot be last-minus-first: that once read 3,587 minutes for an agent that worked 52. Time is classified tool/reason/child/stalled so a parked session never counts as work.

needles.needle: A unit of work is not a session
needles.note: /clear and /handoff scatter one branch across many sessions (one spanned 26), and one session covers many branches (one covered six). Transcript metrics join on git branch, and slice records by it.

needles.needle: Each `/build` invocation is its own ledger
needles.note: Merging two /build passes over the same slices makes every slice look like it took a fix round — a real branch read 0% first-pass-green when its two passes were 33% and 100%.

needles.needle: A failure to measure must never block landing the work
needles.note: The run-cost emit is the last step of /verify-build and is strictly advisory; a metrics error is reported in one line, never a reason to leave a PR unopened.

needles.needle: One session is not one branch either
needles.note: A session that touched six branches reports all six as each other's work unless records are sliced by branch; three unrelated branches once reported byte-identical totals.

Measured on a real fleet run: executors averaged 292k tokens of context per turn across 1,801 calls, and cache reads were 97% of the run's raw token bill. A gate log read once is re-sent every remaining turn, so redirecting output to a file and reading the tail is a cost rule, not only an exit-code rule.

needles.needle: Name a model on every dispatch
needles.note: An unnamed model is not a neutral default — it is the session's, the most expensive one available, silently applied to a role that may need none of it.
The verifier stays on opus: it is the only gate positioned to catch a confidently-wrong oracle, and it is ~11% of a run's cost, so there is nothing to win by cheapening it.

Every fix round is classified before it is dispatched (oracle-wrong / design-silent / ripple / invariant / mis-routed / flake). First-pass green is already measured; the rate alone names no fix, the classification is what turns it into a change to /plan or to a slice's gates.

The optional per-slice `model:` field routes the executor. /plan is the only step that knows which slices are mechanical; an unrouted slices.yaml sends the whole build through the most expensive model available.

A unit agent runs a whole pipeline in one context — the longest-lived in the flow — and its children inherit the session model unless the brief states the routing. Effort cannot be routed at all; it is a pre-flight decision made once for every lane. (Re-pinned 2026-09-05: the constraint-shaped rewrite in 1aa0c3c kept the fact and dropped the literal — the earlier needle was `A lane inherits your model`.)

needles.needle: Splitting is not a token optimisation
needles.note: An artifact's own text is 1-4% of a typical agent's per-turn context (~210k measured); cache reads were 97% of raw tokens. Split for attention, which is scarce; if the stated reason is cost, the lever is elsewhere.

needles.needle: The base flow plugin stays store-agnostic
needles.note: The coupling invariant behind the whole experience-layer overlay: it is a third plugin with its own hooks.json and zero edits to any existing command, because store logic inside /verify-build would be carried by every repo that will never run a store. See docs/adr/ADR-002.

needles.needle: artifacts are about to be destroyed
needles.note: The capture hook keys on worktree teardown, never on `merged`. The ticket asked for `the command that closes the PR` and no such command exists — /verify-build OPENS PRs, and gh pr merge / --delete-branch / git branch -d / git push --delete return zero matches across the base plugin. A matcher aimed at merge would have fired never.

The measured threat model: the .work/ census was 893 files across 6 repos and 101 nine hours later, because one fleet worktree holding 818 files was torn down mid-run, destroying ~30 *.design-draft.md / *.open-forks.md files with nothing capturing them. It fired during its own design run.

needles.needle: there is no command-level matcher in the platform
needles.note: hooks.json's `matcher` selects on the TOOL NAME only. A design table rendering the matcher as `runtime command matches git worktree remove` describes a mechanism that does not exist; written in as a regex it matches no tool and fires never. All discrimination happens inside the hook, on tool_input.command, tokenised — not by substring, because tool_input.description is agent-written prose.

The capture natural key is a pure function of the invocation (the worktree path as written, or the PR URL gh printed). Nothing time-, run- or session-derived may enter it: a key carrying a timestamp makes every re-run a new record and the idempotence claim false. The oracle asserts byte-identical argv across two runs.

needles.needle: A marker that survives a new `/start` is worse than no marker
needles.note: Seam A (ESAS-94). Every `.work/` observable is accumulating residue that is never erased, so a `/design` re-run mid-build was indistinguishable from `/build`. The clearing is the load-bearing half, not the writing: absent, you know you do not know; stale, you are confidently wrong about which work item you are on.

needles.needle: zero providers is the normal case
needles.note: Seam B (ESAS-94). The `/design` Step 1 extension point ships no provider. The no-provider path must be SILENT, not merely harmless — a seam that announces itself in every repo not using it has become the interruption it was designed to avoid, which is exactly how the `esas-pending.sh` hook failed.

The standing rule suppressing the UserPromptSubmit count hook, re-pinned by ESAS-94 because ADR-003 and CONTEXT-PROVIDERS.md now both quote it as the MEASURED EVIDENCE for rejecting hook injection as a context-delivery mechanism. This codebase built that surface, found it an interruption, and suppressed it; the quote is load-bearing in three artifacts now, so losing it loses the reason a rejected option stays rejected.

needles.needle: a hook cannot enter Step 3's reasoning
needles.note: ADR-003 (ESAS-94). The hard limit that forced two seams into the BASE plugin rather than an overlay: a hook fires around a tool call, an MCP call cannot see the slash command, and the place a contribution must land is a fork in an interview. Without this, the next reader re-proposes the overlay-only design that cannot work.

ADR-005 (XL-27). A reused pool worktree is switched to the task-branch tip, cleaned, installed and built before EVERY slice, whether or not anything changed: a reused tree inherits stale .tsbuildinfo and stray compiled .js shadowing sources (remote-ai-agents D6). Skipping the install because the lockfile did not move turns a cost in time into a cost in correctness.

needles.needle: is the single writer of `decisions.md` and `build-summary.md`
needles.note: ADR-005 (XL-27). Only /build's orchestrator writes the committed record; executors, verifiers and pool workers report decisions and facts in their result. Every worker appending to one file would make every cherry-pick of a pool land conflict (design critique C1).
ADR-005 (XL-27). Concerns fail closed: a hard concern that is partial, unmet, cannot-determine or unruled is a failure, never a pass. What the verifier could not check is cannot-determine, never met.

ADR-005 (XL-27). concerns-check's outcome=error (malformed file, missing file, fabricated or foreign waiver citation) is read as failure exactly like fail, never as a pass or as 'no concerns' — the fail-closed half a reader is most likely to soften.

ADR-005 (XL-27). A concern is waived only in the owner's own words, recorded as a decisions.md entry with kind: waiver and decidedBy: human whose title names the concern, and concerns-check --decisions verifies the citation against the unit's own decisions.md. An agent never waives on its own judgment.

needles.needle: This command is the hard block
needles.note: ADR-005 (XL-27). The flow/concerns commit status is advisory (a private free-plan repo cannot require it, and a post can fail); /merge-multi runs concerns-check itself on each unit head and refuses to merge anything but outcome=pass (design critique C2).

needles.needle: a continued agent never takes another slice
needles.note: A fix round continued with SendMessage stays in the transcript it resumes: run-metrics attributes by dispatch description and counts each resume as a pass, so an agent resumed onto another slice bills its whole life to the first (one verifier resumed across ten slices did).
Re-check mode judges each finding against the fix-round diff, never the executor's response — the narrowed pass must not become a relay of 'fixed'.

needles.needle: The cap exists for the fix round, not the first pass
needles.note: /plan splits a slice over 10 files or 200 call/string sites, counted at the base, unless it is atomic: one finding in an oversize sweep re-opens the whole sweep (TV2-21's ~26-file billing sweep ran 3 h 20 m and escalated).

needles.needle: never when the gap is the slice's own oracle
needles.note: An environment gap (unbuilt sibling, missing credential, sandbox refusal) is reported, not escalated, and a slice may PASS on what did run — but an oracle that cannot run is a red mechanical gate, so the gap is never an escape for the slice's own test.

needles.needle: names which Step 2 branch sent a `sequential` slice
needles.note: Every main-tree slice records modeReason: TV2-21's pool sized width 4 and every slice ran sequentially with nothing saying why.

needles.needle: Only a contribution the provider marks canonical may settle a fork
needles.note: XL-67 D3: a pending, backfilled or text-only contribution is a candidate that OPENS a fork and never closes one; only one the provider marks canonical can be cited as what settled it.

XL-67 F4: a context provider is declared by the host repo in .claude/bett3r-ai-workflow.json. Tool presence is a sniff, not a declaration, and a capture marker cannot say whether a repo wants design-time grounding.

needles.needle: a claim about the corpus where all you have is an outage
needles.note: XL-67 D9/F2: a provider that refuses or times out degrades to one `grounding degraded:` note and the fork stays open with a reason. An outage and an empty corpus are different facts and are never conflated.

needles.needle: a citation that lives only in the draft is destroyed by the next regeneration
needles.note: XL-67 F1: the citation for what settled a fork rides on the fork's map status under resolvedBy, not in prose, because ADR-007 makes regenerated decision text a projection of the map.

needles.needle: that id has one home: the sidecar the verdict names
needles.note: XL-70 F3: the id a recorder hands back for an answered fork lives in the fork-id-keyed sidecar beside map.json and nowhere else. map.json itself never carries it — the fork status is additionalProperties:false and refs the byte-identical copy of esas's vocabulary, so an id in the map is a cross-repo vocabulary change.
XL-70 F1: argument derivation lives in design-map, not in command prose, so every field of the payload is testable with nothing reachable. The verb posts nothing; the caller makes the declared call.

needles.needle: Never probe whether the provider is up before calling
needles.note: XL-70 F4, dissolved on ADR-053's Principle: a rule an agent must follow across commands belongs in the one process every command calls, as a typed refusal — never restated as a health check in each command's prompt. The command degrades on RECEIVING a refusal.

needles.needle: as this lane's own resolution, never as the owner's
needles.note: XL-70 R1: a lane passes nothing asserting whether it is attended — that is derived from the marked worktree by the process the call goes to. A lane that could claim otherwise could sign its own guesses as the owner's answers.

The measured cost of a lane that ran all five pipeline steps in one context: 9.7h, +2164/-259 lines, 89% cache read. The number is the whole argument for step-lane and sliceBudget; without it the shape reads as taste.
Same fleet, same day: the same work handed to a FRESH context at a step boundary cost an order of magnitude less than the accumulating one. The controlled comparison, not just the bad number.

needles.needle: The saving is not the dispatch, it is the **ending**
needles.note: Why a step-lane must run exactly one step. A context that ends stops being re-read; an agent that helpfully runs two steps rebuilds the accumulation it was created to delete.
The only guard on the /build yield loop: a budget yield that resumes onto the same slice forever is the one way the loop burns more than it saves.

Why sliceBudget counts slices and not tokens: a step cannot see its own usage (run-metrics measures it afterwards, too late to act on), so the ceiling must be in a unit countable from inside, at a clean resume point.

needles.needle: second axis, and it is not a machine resource
needles.note: Fleet sizing was reasoned entirely in memory, cores and swap. Five lanes fit in RAM comfortably and consumed most of a weekly allowance in six hours: machine headroom and spend are uncorrelated, and only one of them was ever written down.

needles.needle: one local worktree and nowhere else
needles.note: Why /build pushes every slice instead of once at the end. Until /verify-build step 6 a lane's commits exist only on the machine that made them, so a rate-limit kill, a cost stop or a reclaimed worktree loses every green slice already paid for. A slice costs minutes to earn; the push costs seconds.

The promotion boundary. A decided fork's walk becomes a slice oracle, so a prose walk is refused there rather than downstream: `oracle-wrong` was 41% of 966 classified fix rounds, every itemised one caught by the verifier and none by a red test, and RED -> GREEN structurally cannot catch it — a test built from prose goes red before the code exists and green after, and is still wrong.

A decided fork whose chosen option carries no walk was a silent counter (`skipped-nowalk`). It is a choice somebody made that nobody can test, and its slice gets an oracle invented downstream from prose.

The half of the walk contract that reaches a unit with NO map.json — which is what both measured 0%-first-pass-green runs were (`review: unattended`, no map), so the candidate pipeline emitted nothing and fifteen slices' oracles were written freehand.

Given/When/Then has no room for a census's negative half ("and no module outside <owner> does Y"), and that half is what catches the writer added next week — it caught a composition root whose two wiring lines could both be deleted with tsc clean and 738 tests green.

The seams are named ONCE per unit, before any oracle — fewest, highest, existing over new, the ideal number one (Pocock, `to-spec`). His gate is a human confirm; fleet lanes are unattended by construction, so the seam is named, located and defended instead, and check-plan refuses a plan that declares none.

A slice whose oracle sits at a seam the unit never declared. /plan wrote a per-slice oracle under no pressure toward a shared seam, so eight slices invented eight oracle locations — each an independent chance to assert below the level the claim lives at, which is the shape of the worst defect in the corpus.

Fewest is pressure, not a cap: the first seam is free, every seam after it and every `kind: new` one owes one line saying why the named seams cannot hold the claim. A cap would be wrong — some units genuinely need two — but silence was what was wrong before.

REACHABILITY. The slice names, at plan time, the one production line whose deletion must turn its oracle red — before a test exists that has to survive it, since a probe named afterwards is invented to fit what was built. An erasure suite that composed its own subject stayed 8/8 green with the production harness spread removed, and PII shipped unencrypted with every gate green.

TAUTOLOGY. An assertion that recomputes its expected value the way the code does passes by construction and can never disagree with the code — red before the code exists and green after, so RED -> GREEN structurally cannot catch it. The expected value comes from a known-good literal, a worked example or the spec, and everything but a literal cites where: the citation is the check.

DISCRIMINATION. A RED that is a hang, timeout, crash, import error, empty collection or skipped suite is indistinguishable from a broken harness and is no evidence the test can tell right from wrong. It is a property of the run, not the plan, so it is enforced where that evidence exists rather than claimed by a YAML field.

Pocock's retro rule, as the DEFAULT disposition of a repeat fix-round cause: classify the violation first — a mechanical one (a fixed syntactic pattern, a banned API, an import shape, a file-location rule) gets a check, and prose is reserved for genuine judgement calls. Writing the rule down a second time changes nothing about the run that would have broken it; every fix round was already classified and the tally was quoted in retros and disposed of by nobody.

A standard is imposed by the REVIEW agent, not the implementation agent: the implementer is under the most context pressure at exactly the moment it would have to remember the rule. So a judgement disposition goes where the verifier reads and a mechanical one goes in scripts/ — never one more line in the executor's brief.
